summary: The Notion REST API lets connections (integrations) read and write Notion pages, databases/data sources, blocks, comments, users and files. It uses JSON over HTTPS, bearer-token auth, cursor-based pagination, date-based versioning via a required header, and webhooks for change events.

sources.quote: The base URL to send all API requests is https://api.notion.com.

value.description: Bearer token: internal connection API token, OAuth access token from a public connection, or a personal access token.

sources.quote: A bearer token is required to interact with the Notion API.

value.description: Pass next_cursor as start_cursor (query string for GET, body for POST); page_size max 100. Treat cursors as opaque.

sources.quote: Endpoints that return lists of objects support cursor-based pagination requests.

value.limits: Per connection: 600 req/min (Business/Enterprise), 180 req/min (other plans); plus a shared per-workspace limit and some per-endpoint limits
value.description: Exceeding returns HTTP 429 rate_limited (529 service_overload when overloaded) with additional_data.rate_limit_reason; respect Retry-After. Limits may change.

sources.quote: Connections should handle HTTP 429 and 529 responses and respect the Retry-After response header.

value.signatureVerification: Not seen in the fetched (truncated) page; see the Webhooks overview page.
value.description: Webhooks are signals only, so fetch the latest data via the API. Some events are aggregated, delivery is not ordered, and up to 8 retries over about 24 hours.

sources.quote: we will retry delivery up to 8 times using an exponential backoff schedule

value.description: JSON error object with object=error, HTTP status, a stable string code, a message, and optional additional_data (e.g. retry guidance, rate_limit_reason).
value.example: {"object":"error","status":503,"code":"service_unavailable","message":"The change was saved, but the response could not be built in time. Read the object again instead of repeating the write.","additional_data":{...}}

sources.quote: Error responses contain more detail about the error in the response body, in the "code" and "message" properties.

value.description: Date-named versions set via the required Notion-Version header. Backwards-incompatible changes get a new version, additive changes ship to all versions. Opt-in betas use a Notion-Beta header. URL /v1 is unrelated to versioning.

sources.quote: Set the version by including a Notion-Version header. Setting this header is required.

risks.title: Write may succeed despite 503
risks.detail: A write can save and still return 503. Check additional_data.retry_guidance and read the object before retrying, or you may duplicate it.

risks.title: Webhook events are signals only and unordered
risks.detail: Events are aggregated, may arrive out of order, and carry no full content. Re-fetch current state and order by timestamp.

risks.title: Rate limits are shared and may change
risks.detail: There is also a per-workspace limit with Retry-After possibly over a minute, and Notion plans to adjust limits.

risks.title: Notion-Version header required
risks.detail: Requests without it return 400 missing_version. Newer versions (e.g. 2025-09-03 data sources) change endpoints and webhook event types.

risks.title: Resources must be shared with the connection
risks.detail: Unshared resources return 404 object_not_found, which is easily mistaken for a bad ID.

risks.title: Payload size limits
risks.detail: Maximum 1000 blocks and 500KB per request, plus property-level limits (e.g. 2000 characters of rich text).

risks.title: Several endpoint paths unverified
risks.detail: Only 5 pages were fetched, so most endpoint paths and parameters were not read from the reference pages.
